## Permissive research handoff

Immutable period: Putin, Russian Federation, 2000.

I recovered additional defensible evidence and preserved the attribution and temporal limits. No ruler score is assigned.

### New or repaired source-claim units

- `RU2000-NUC-10` — SIPRI’s *Yearbook 2000* reports Russia’s January 2000 deployed strategic warheads as 3,540 land-based, 1,576 sea-based, and 790 aircraft warheads; it estimates Russia’s total stockpile at over 22,000 warheads, including strategic, tactical, reserve, and awaiting-dismantlement weapons. Precise locator: pp. 18–19, table and explanatory notes. This is a Russia-specific 2000 arsenal baseline, not evidence of Putin’s personal command quality. Contrary: estimates include categories with uncertain operational status. Links: 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.10. [SIPRI Yearbook 2000](https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2016-03/SIPRIYB00mini.pdf)

- `RU2000-CH-11` — Human Rights Watch reported on 5 April 2000 that Russian investigations into Chechen atrocities were not credible; an earlier investigation into the Aldi massacre found no Russian soldiers accountable despite survivor testimony implicating Russian forces. Precise locator: press release paragraphs 17–26. Attribution: Russian investigative institutions and government response, not proof Putin ordered abuses. Contrary: this records institutional failure, not direct presidential intent. Links: 2B.9, 3B.4, 3B.9, 7B.7. [HRW, 5 April 2000](https://www.hrw.org/legacy/press/2000/04/chech0405.htm)

- `RU2000-CH-12` — HRW’s September 2000 accountability memorandum states that Russia had made no meaningful progress, had not created an independent inquiry, and had not established accountability or prevented impunity. Precise locator: paragraphs 21–27. Attribution: Russian government response; Putin attribution is authority-based but not personal-direction evidence. Contrary: Putin had appointed a special human-rights representative, whose office provided some detainee-release and documentation assistance. Links: 2B.9, 3B.4, 7B.7. [HRW memorandum](https://www.hrw.org/legacy/press/2000/09/russia0905-memo.htm)

- `RU2000-CH-13` — HRW’s account based on a November 2000 field mission records that military prosecutors had opened 35 cases against federal servicemen by December 2000, but investigations were delayed, weak, and produced no criminal accountability for the documented Alkhan-Yurt, Staropromyslovski, and Novye Aldi killings by the end of the period. Precise locator: paragraphs 44–57 and 61–75. Period fit: in-period facts reported in a February 2001 publication. Attribution: government accountability machinery; not evidence of a personal Putin order. Contrary: the Budanov case was publicly acknowledged and pursued, although its investigation concluded only in 2001. Links: 2B.9, 3B.4, 3B.9, 7B.2. [HRW domestic-prosecutions memorandum](https://www.hrw.org/legacy/backgrounder/eca/chechmemo-0213.htm)

- `RU2000-6B-05` — The World Bank records that the Russian government adopted a ten-year development plan in July 2000 with objectives covering vulnerable households, universal access to basic health and education, social-spending redistribution, pension sustainability, and targeted housing benefits. Precise locator: pp. 28–29, lines 1066–1105. Attribution: government program under Putin’s administration; this establishes planning, not completed implementation. Contrary: the report explicitly says implementation required sustained future political commitment. Links: 6B.1, 6B.2, 6B.5, 6B.9, 8B.1, 8B.2. [World Bank report](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/194201468781516144/pdf/multi-page.pdf)

- `RU2000-6B-06` — The same World Bank report records increased minimum pensions, increased education allocations, and reduced wage arrears during the preceding year, while noting that pensions remained below pre-crisis real levels and health interventions were still developing. Precise locator: p. 13, lines 475–502. Period fit: outcome evidence covering 2000, published January 2001. Attribution: government-level, not personally Putin-attributed. Contrary: modest improvements coexisted with unresolved social deterioration. Links: 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.9, 6B.10. [World Bank report](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/194201468781516144/pdf/multi-page.pdf)

### Existing units to retain or normalize

- Retain `RU2000-4B-05` through `RU2000-4B-09` from the supervisor takeover, using the OSCE/ODIHR PDF page-and-line locators. These provide precise election-quality, counting, Chechen-access, campaign-administration, and NTV/Media Most evidence, but remain state/administrative evidence rather than proof of Putin’s personal approval.

- Retain `RU2000-7B-05` for the exact Transparency International CPI 2000 score of 2.1. Keep it as institutional context only; it does not establish personal dishonesty or enrichment.

- Retain `RU2000-NUC-07` and `RU2000-NUC-08` as institutional nuclear-security evidence. Together with `RU2000-NUC-10`, they close much of the Russia-specific posture gap, but none establishes Putin’s personal nuclear oversight.

### Dispositions unchanged

- The 1998 strategic-force inventory remains `context`, not 2000 inventory evidence.
- The 2001 Chechen termination declaration, later flat-tax revenue effects, and later accountability findings remain excluded from 2000 outcome claims.
- Putin/family enrichment in 2000 remains `no_evidence_found`; no substitute claim is inferred from oligarch arrangements or corruption indicators.
